claim.value: Missing entries can contribute to obtaining different minimal subsets.
claim.scope: Possible effect of incomplete records on reduction results.

provenance.rationale: The span explicitly identifies missing entries as a possible contributor to different minimal subsets.

signal_basis.value: The procedure reconstructs configurations from records while retaining missing information as unknown, then tests reductions for repeated failure. Smaller configurations can preserve lateness while specified further removals cease to reproduce it; uncertain or inconsistent tests remain unresolved.
signal_basis.scope: Reduction results for the selected reconstructed case under the fixed test conditions and predeclared repetition rule.

provenance.rationale: These spans establish incomplete reconstruction, controlled reduction tests, the reproduction pattern and treatment of unresolved outcomes.
The bounded possibility claim is supported without an additional unresolved empirical relation.

rationale: Reduction results depend on the reconstructed configuration and test conditions. Missing records can leave relevant components or conditions undetermined, permitting different reconstructions and consequently different minimal subsets. This licenses the claimed possibility without establishing that missing entries actually changed any particular result.
uncertainty: The signal does not establish whether missing entries affected this case or which alternative subsets would result.
